title: Designing Tables
projectGoals: Entities: customers, addresses, products, categories, product_categories, inventory, carts, cart_items, orders, order_items, payments, shipments
Rules: unique SKU; non-negative prices and stock; quantity > 0; historical unit price snapshot; valid order/payment states; deliberate delete behavior
Artifacts: ER diagram, data dictionary, migrations, seed data, 20 SQL queries, constraint tests
acceptance: No repeating product columns
No invalid foreign keys
Historical order totals do not change when catalogue prices change

title: Making Queries Fast
blurb: Performance optimization with plans and indexes.
projectGoals: Generate 50k–100k products with realistic category, price, status, name and timestamp distributions
Workload: SKU lookup; category + active + newest; price range; name search; category counts
Baseline with EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS); add ONE index at a time; compare plans, latency, buffers and write cost
Try composite/partial B-tree, lower(name) expression index, GIN for full-text / JSONB
acceptance: Report the slowest 3 queries
Chosen indexes with measured impact
Indexes rejected because they did not help

title: Transactions
projectGoals: POST /orders with idempotency key, stock validation/reservation, order + items, rollback on failure
Transaction + row locking or a carefully designed conditional UPDATE; check affected-row counts
Tests: two concurrent requests for the final unit, duplicate retries, simulated failure, payment-provider timeout (separately)
acceptance: No negative stock
No duplicate order for the same idempotency key
No partially committed order

title: Scaling
projectGoals: Diagram primary + read replica + cache + backup/WAL; label read/write paths and consistency requirements
Workload assumptions: active users, req/s, read/write ratio, growth, peak, availability target
Compare in order: vertical scaling, pooling, indexing, partitioning, read replicas, sharding
Define RPO/RTO, failover, replica-lag handling, restore drills, shard key, hot-key mitigation, rebalancing
acceptance: Architecture decision record
Assumptions, bottlenecks, failure modes
Phased scaling plan

title: Django & API Engineering
blurb: The framework layer interviews probe next: ORM, APIs, background jobs and security.
projectGoals: Products, cart, checkout (POST /orders with an Idempotency-Key), order history and admin product updates
DRF with cursor pagination, ordering allowlists, object-level permissions and throttling
assertNumQueries on every list endpoint; versioned migrations including a concurrent index
Celery for post-order work using on_commit and idempotent tasks; Redis cache-aside with invalidation
manage.py check --deploy clean; CSRF and CORS configured deliberately
Docker Compose, structured logs, health checks; unit, integration, concurrency and API tests
acceptance: No N+1 on list endpoints, proved by tests
Concurrent checkout never oversells and a repeated Idempotency-Key never creates a second order
check --deploy passes and no endpoint exposes another user's data
README with setup, architecture diagram and benchmark results

title: Behavioral interviews
projectGoals: Write 5 STAR stories (conflict, failure, deadline, ownership, ambiguity) with real numbers in the Result
acceptance: Every STAR story has a measurable result and says what YOU did
You can tell each story in two minutes without notes

title: Python and Django internals
blurb: What happens inside Python and inside a Django request.
projectGoals: A custom middleware that logs method, path, status and duration for every request
Login with Django sessions for the browser and a token endpoint for API clients
Tests with the Django test client that cover a successful request, a rejected request and a middleware short-circuit
acceptance: You can draw the request path from server to view and back, naming each layer
A request without credentials is rejected before the view runs, proven by a test
No mutable default arguments remain in the code or model fields
You can explain when you would choose sessions, tokens or JWT for this service

title: Git, containers and deployment
blurb: From a commit to a running service.
projectGoals: A Dockerfile that orders layers so a code change does not reinstall dependencies, plus a .dockerignore
A compose file that runs the web app, Postgres and Redis together
A CI workflow that runs the tests on every push and blocks a failing change
Run the app with Gunicorn behind Nginx locally and pass python manage.py check --deploy
acceptance: A fresh clone starts the whole stack with one command
Editing one line of code rebuilds in seconds because dependency layers are cached
A deliberately broken test makes the pipeline fail before any deploy step
Secrets come from the environment and are not in the repository or the image

title: Browser, React and performance
blurb: The runtime, the rendering model, and what users feel.
projectGoals: Build a searchable list and a detail view in React with loading, empty and error states
Debounce the search input and cancel stale requests
Measure the page with a performance tool and fix the largest problem you find
Make every control reachable and usable by keyboard, with labels and visible focus
acceptance: You can explain why each re-render happened using props, state and keys
The page has no console errors and handles a slow or failing API gracefully
You recorded a before and after number for one performance fix
A keyboard-only run through the main flow works

title: Analytics SQL and pipelines
blurb: Answer questions in SQL, then automate the answers reliably.
projectGoals: Load a CSV or API source into Postgres idempotently so a re-run changes nothing
Write window-function and CTE queries for a ranking, a running total and a month-over-month change
Add data-quality checks (row counts, nulls, duplicates) that fail the run
Schedule it with a simple orchestrator or cron and log each run
acceptance: Running the pipeline twice for the same day gives identical results
A deliberately bad input file is caught by a check before it reaches the final table
Each query has a note on its grain (one row per what?)
You can explain batch versus streaming for this data

title: Reliability and operations
blurb: Know when a service is unhealthy, and act well when it is.
projectGoals: Expose request count, error count and latency metrics from a small service
Define one SLI and an SLO for it and compute the remaining error budget from your data
Declare a small piece of infrastructure as code and review its plan before applying
Cause a failure on purpose, handle it as an incident, and write a blameless postmortem
acceptance: Your SLO has a number, a time window and a measurable SLI
The postmortem lists a timeline, impact, causes and concrete follow-up actions
Infrastructure changes show a reviewed plan before they are applied
An alert fires on a symptom users would feel, not only on a machine metric

title: Models and ML systems
blurb: Evaluate honestly, deploy carefully, monitor continuously.
project: Train, evaluate and monitor a classifier
projectGoals: Split data into train and test (and validate with cross-validation) before touching the test set
Report precision, recall and a confusion matrix, and explain which one matters for your problem
Serve the model behind a simple API and log its inputs and predictions
Detect a simulated input drift and describe your rollback plan
acceptance: The test set was used once, at the end
You can explain overfitting using your own training and validation scores
A drifted batch of inputs triggers an alert or a failed check
You can state a baseline the model must beat to be worth shipping

title: System design
blurb: The building blocks (caching, load balancing, queues, consistency, CDN, communication) and the classic designs (feed, chat, crawler, key-value store, notifications, file sync, video, proximity, payments).
project: Scale a small Django service and measure it
projectGoals: Run two app processes behind a load balancer (nginx or similar) and show a login works whichever process answers
Add cache-aside to one hot read with a TTL, then record the hit rate and the database queries before and after
Move one slow task to a queue with an idempotent worker and show it survives being delivered twice
Add a per-user rate limit that answers 429 with a Retry-After header
Write a one-page design for a URL shortener: numbers, data model, the read path and what you would cache
Design, on paper and in 35 minutes each, a news feed, a chat system and a payment system using the six-step framework, with the numbers and the trade-offs written down
Estimate, for one of them, requests per second, storage per year and bandwidth, and state the decision each number drives
acceptance: You can draw, from memory, the path of a read through load balancer, cache and database, and say what is stale at each step
A load test shows the cache hit rate and the drop in database load, with the numbers written down
Killing one app process does not log users out or lose queued work
You can explain, with one example each, a retry storm, a cache stampede and a split brain, and the usual fix for each
You can run the six-step framework aloud for a new prompt and finish the high-level design within 20 minutes

title: Data structures and algorithms
blurb: The structures and patterns behind most coding questions, each with the cost you must state.
projectGoals: Solve at least 4 problems for each of: hash maps, stacks and queues, linked lists, sorting and binary search, trees, graphs, heaps, backtracking and dynamic programming, in plain Python, without looking up the answer first
For every problem write the brute-force complexity, the improved time and space, and the edge cases you tested
Re-solve five problems you got wrong, a week later, from a blank file
acceptance: Each solved problem has a note stating time and space complexity
You can explain two-sum from brute force to hash map in under two minutes
You can write merge sort, binary search, BFS and a memoized recursion from memory
You have timed yourself solving one medium problem in 30 minutes, with tests

title: Low-level design
blurb: Classes, relationships and methods that are easy to change.
project: Three designs with code and tests
projectGoals: Design and code a library system (members, books, loans, late fees) using the six-step method
Implement an LRU cache from a dict and a doubly linked list, without OrderedDict
Model an elevator or an order status as a state machine and test every transition
acceptance: Each design starts from written requirements and has a class and relationship sketch
Adding a new requirement (a member type, a pricing rule, a state) edits no existing working class
Every design has tests for the main flow and at least one error case, and a note on concurrency

title: Operating systems, concurrency and networking
blurb: The fundamentals interviewers ask about by name, each with a runnable simulation.
project: Simulate it: a scheduler, a page replacer and a thread-safe bank
projectGoals: Simulate FIFO, shortest-job-first and round robin for a set of jobs and report average turnaround and response time
Count page faults for FIFO and LRU on a reference string with 3 and 4 frames, and show Belady's anomaly
Write a thread-safe bank account with transfer(), take locks in a global order, and test with 8 threads that the total stays constant
acceptance: You can compute turnaround and response time for a small job set by hand and match your code
A test shows a lost update without a lock and the correct total with one
You can explain deadlock, its four conditions and one way to prevent it
